title: MySQL Router and Connection Routing knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes “MySQL Router and Connection Routing”?
options: It is a frontend styling feature and does not involve database behavior.
It guarantees correct output regardless of schema, permissions, or release version.
It is best handled by removing constraints and skipping error checks.

An application connection is a trust boundary. Keep credentials outside source control, use parameterized queries for values, define transaction boundaries, and handle lost connections without assuming a request was never committed.
questions.answer_key: An application connection is a trust boundary. Keep credentials outside source control, use parameterized queries for values, define transaction boundaries, and handle lost connections without assuming a request was never committed.
questions.explanation: The lesson explains: An application connection is a trust boundary. Keep credentials outside source control, use parameterized queries for values, define transaction boundaries, and handle lost connections without assuming a request was never committed.

questions.prompt: Which practice best applies “MySQL Router and Connection Routing” safely?
options: Concatenate untrusted input into SQL text and grant administrator privileges to every application user.
Judge success only by whether the statement returns any rows, without checking expected behavior or edge cases.
Perform a local connection check, identify the selected server/account, and record the command output without including passwords.
Skip testing, assume every SQL engine behaves identically, and apply the change directly to production.
questions.answer_key: Perform a local connection check, identify the selected server/account, and record the command output without including passwords.
questions.explanation: Perform a local connection check, identify the selected server/account, and record the command output without including passwords. This makes the result reviewable and aligns with a controlled learning workflow.

questions.prompt: Before relying on an example for “MySQL Router and Connection Routing”, what should be verified?
options: Assume a successful connection means the query and data model are correct.
Confirm the exact MySQL version and prerequisites, predict the result, run a minimal test in a disposable environment, then inspect the evidence and relevant official documentation.
Run a broad production change before checking the current state.
Ignore version notes and infer behavior from an unrelated database engine.
questions.answer_key: Confirm the exact MySQL version and prerequisites, predict the result, run a minimal test in a disposable environment, then inspect the evidence and relevant official documentation.
questions.explanation: Confirm the exact MySQL version and prerequisites, predict the result, run a minimal test in a disposable environment, then inspect the evidence and relevant official documentation. The CodeLeaf editor displays reference output only; real behavior depends on the selected server/runtime.
